issues.title: Missing braces in for loop
issues.description: The rule requires all control flow statements (if, else, for, foreach, while, do-while) to use curly braces even for single-line bodies, but the inner for loop omits curly braces
issues.rule_name: Use Curly Braces for All Control Flow Statements

issues.title: Inverted renderer type check prevents circuit restart
issues.description: The condition checking for different renderer types has been inverted from `!==` to `===`. This causes the function to throw an error when the SAME renderer type tries to re-enable JS root components (e.g., during circuit restart), which is the exact scenario that should be allowed. The original intent was to throw an error only when a DIFFERENT renderer type attempts to enable root components. This bug breaks circuit restart functionality, causing applications to fail when users reconnect after a circuit disconnect.

issues.title: Missing parameter update causes stale data on circuit restart
issues.description: The assignment `jsComponentParametersByIdentifier = jsComponentParameters;` has been removed from the re-enabling logic. When a circuit restarts and `enableJSRootComponents` is called again with new parameters, the global `jsComponentParametersByIdentifier` is not updated. This causes the application to continue using stale parameters from the previous circuit. The `DynamicRootComponent` class constructor and methods rely on `jsComponentParametersByIdentifier` to retrieve component parameter definitions, so they will operate with outdated metadata after a circuit restart.

issues.title: Test method missing Arrange/Act/Assert comments
issues.description: The added test method does not contain explicit '// Arrange', '// Act', and '// Assert' (or '// Act & Assert') comments to delineate the AAA phases, violating the required test structure convention.
issues.rule_name: Test Methods Must Use Arrange-Act-Assert Pattern with Comments

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #64536 - Allow JS root components to reinitialize on circuit restart

structured_output.summary:
The PR lets JS root components be re-enabled when a new Blazor circuit starts on the same page, instead of throwing 'Dynamic root components have already been enabled.' It changes enableJSRootComponents to take a rendererId, skips the JS custom-element initializers after the first run (hasInitializedJsComponents), and accepts the new manager DotNetObjectReference. It also moves the PersistentStateIsSupportedInDynamicJSRoots E2E test back into StatePersistenceTest.cs, deletes StatePersistanceJSRootTest.cs, and always registers the dynamic-js-root-counter component in RazorComponentEndpointsStartup.

As written, the change does not work. The renderer guard is inverted: it throws when the renderer ID matches, which is exactly the circuit-restart case the PR is meant to support, and it silently accepts a different renderer, which the comment and PR description say must throw. Separately, the line that assigns jsComponentParametersByIdentifier was dropped during the refactor, so that map is never populated. Blazor.rootComponents.add() reads from it on every call, so the test page's add() would throw a TypeError even on the first circuit. The test move itself is clean, but the test suite does not exercise the restart or multi-host paths, so nothing here would catch these defects.
structured_output.verdictRationale: Two correctness defects in JSRootComponents.ts each break the feature on their own: the inverted renderer guard (blocks restart, allows multi-host) and the missing parameters assignment (breaks Blazor.rootComponents.add() entirely). The E2E test that was moved would fail on the first load for the second reason. These need fixing before merge.

architecture.overview:
Dynamic JS root components are a Blazor feature where page JavaScript calls Blazor.rootComponents.add() to render a .NET component into a container. On startup, the framework calls enableJSRootComponents (via attachWebRendererInterop in WebRendererInteropMethods.ts) with the renderer ID, a DotNetObjectReference 'manager' for the circuit, the per-component parameter metadata, and the custom-element initializers. The JS module keeps a module-level manager, a renderer ID, and the parameter map, and add() / DynamicRootComponent use them to call back into .NET.

The PR changes that enable step. It now records the renderer ID and accepts a new manager when the same renderer type enables again (a new circuit or a restart), and it runs the initializers only once. The intent is to allow a restart without an error, while still rejecting a second, different host on the same page. The test asset moves from a conditional registration (--RegisterDynamicJSRootComponent) to an unconditional one in RazorComponentEndpointsStartup.
steps: Entry point: the server-rendered page or WASM host calls attachWebRendererInterop(rendererId, ...) in WebRendererInteropMethods.ts, which builds the manager and calls enableJSRootComponents when JS-registered components exist.

enableJSRootComponents in JSRootComponents.ts now takes rendererId as its first argument. The guard at line 126 decides whether to throw; the PR intends this to fire only for a different renderer type, but the operator is currently reversed.

The manager and currentRendererId are updated (lines 136-137). The parameter map (jsComponentParametersByIdentifier) is supposed to be set here too, but that assignment was removed, so it stays undefined.
Initializers run once, gated by hasInitializedJsComponents (lines 139-150), so custom elements are not re-registered on a new circuit.
Blazor.rootComponents.add() (line 30) reads the parameter map and the manager to create DynamicRootComponent instances; the test page dynamic-js-root.html exercises this path.

Test wiring: StatePersistenceTest.cs gains PersistentStateIsSupportedInDynamicJSRoots, the old StatePersistanceJSRootTest.cs is removed, and the test app registers dynamic-js-root-counter for every RazorComponentEndpointsStartup host.

findings.title: Renderer guard is inverted: circuit restart throws, multi-host passes
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/Components/Web.JS/src/Rendering/JSRootComponents.ts`, the guard in `enableJSRootComponents` (around line 126) is inverted. It currently throws when `manager && currentRendererId === rendererId`, which blocks the same-renderer circuit restart the PR is supposed to allow. Change it so it throws only when the renderer type differs (`currentRendererId !== rendererId`), keeping the existing error message. Keep the comments at lines 127-135 consistent with the final behavior.

findings.title: Parameter map is never assigned, so Blazor.rootComponents.add() throws
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/Components/Web.JS/src/Rendering/JSRootComponents.ts`, `enableJSRootComponents` no longer assigns the module-level `jsComponentParametersByIdentifier` (it was dropped during the refactor). Restore `jsComponentParametersByIdentifier = jsComponentParameters;` next to `manager = managerInstance;` (around line 137), so the map is set on every enable call, including restarts. The map is read by `RootComponentsFunctions.add` at line 30. Verify that the initializer block that now sits inside `if (!hasInitializedJsComponents)` still uses the `jsComponentParameters` argument directly and does not depend on this module variable.

findings.title: No test exercises the restart or multi-host behavior this PR is about
findings.fixPrompt: Add coverage for the behavior in `src/Components/Web.JS/src/Rendering/JSRootComponents.ts` that this PR changes. In `src/Components/test/E2ETest/Tests/StatePersistenceTest.cs` (near `PersistentStateIsSupportedInDynamicJSRoots`, lines 279-291), add a test that restarts or reconnects the circuit on the `dynamic-js-root.html` page and checks that the counter renders again with no 'already been enabled' error. Also add a JS-side test that calls `enableJSRootComponents` twice with the same rendererId (must not throw) and with different rendererIds (must throw). Follow the existing test layout in the Web.JS test project.

findings.title: Dynamic root component is now registered for every RazorComponentEndpointsStartup app
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/Components/test/testassets/Components.TestServer/RazorComponentEndpointsStartup.cs` (around line 54), the `RegisterForJavaScript<ComponentWithPersistentState>("dynamic-js-root-counter")` call is now unconditional, so every test app built on this startup enables JS root components. Decide whether that is intended. If it is not, restore the `Configuration.GetValue<bool>("RegisterDynamicJSRootComponent")` guard and make the StatePersistenceTest fixture pass that argument. If it is intended, state in the PR description why all RazorComponentEndpointsStartup apps need the dynamic root registered.

findings.title: Test move and cleanup are done cleanly
findings.body: The E2E test moves from the separate StatePersistanceJSRootTest.cs into StatePersistenceTest.cs, next to the other persistent-state tests, and the now-unused `Components.TestServer` Program.cs entry is removed. The test body is unchanged, and no other file references the removed entry name, so the cleanup is complete.

findings.title: Initializers gated to run once across circuits
findings.body:
Keeping the custom-element initializers behind `hasInitializedJsComponents` is a sensible design. Custom elements can only be registered once per page, so re-running the initializers on each new circuit would throw or re-register. Gating them this way lets a new circuit's manager replace the old one without repeating global side effects.
